reality.qualifier: Consumer Reports 70 mph steady-state highway test, fully charged to depletion. Vehicle is the Extended Range Lariat trim CR purchased anonymously.
reality.verbatim_quote: The recently discontinued Ford F-150 Lightning pickup truck's battery ran out after just 270 miles—a 50-mile difference from the EPA estimate.

sources.name: Consumer Reports — Real-World Electric Car Range Comparison
F-150 Lightning Forum — owner thread with corroborating real-world reports

narrative_one_liner: Ford advertises 320 mi EPA; Consumer Reports' 70 mph highway test measured 270 mi — a 50-mile (16%) gap.
narrative: Ford advertises the Extended Range Lightning at 320 mi EPA. Consumer Reports' instrumented 70 mph highway test measured 270 mi to depletion — a 50-mile, 15.6% gap. This is among the largest gaps CR has documented across 26 EVs they have tested, tied with the Rivian R1S Dual Max. EPA combined-cycle weighting toward city driving inflates the headline relative to real interstate use.
methodology_notes: CR conducts a steady 70 mph highway test on a unit purchased anonymously, with reproduceable methodology published. Owner forum corroboration provides Tier-3 supporting evidence with multiple independent owner reports in the cited thread.
caveats: CR tested a 2022 Extended Range Lariat trim; we apply the result to 2024 ER on assumption that powertrain and battery are unchanged. Verified via EPA filings — unchanged.
Single-unit Tier-2 test; would benefit from corroboration by Out of Spec Reviews or InsideEVs instrumented test.
alternative_explanations: Cold weather adds further range loss; CR's test conditions are documented as moderate (not winter).
Tire choice: extended-range Lightnings ship with all-season Pirelli Scorpion 22-inch wheels by default; varying these would shift efficiency.
